Are you eager to join a growing biotech company of currently about 25 enthusiastic employees? Enduro Genetics is a world-leading biotech at the interface of synthetic biology and biomanufacturing with Enduro Sense, a transformative gene technology that redefines the capabilities of cells in fermentation. Enduro Sense is used for cell-based expression systems and production strains to deliver higher titer, rate and yields, making biomanufacturing more efficient and scalable.

We work with industrial clients who biomanufacture products using bacteria and yeasts to make their great processes even better.

The role

We are looking for a Senior Fermentation Scientist with industrial scale-up experience to help our clients get Enduro Sense working in their processes at scale.

jobs.occupation: Monitoring and Evaluation Advisor for DIGNITY’s international programmes
jobs.description:
Would you like to work in an organisation that makes a tangible and positive difference for vulnerable people in Denmark and globally? If so, DIGNITY can offer you an exciting opportunity as MEAL Advisor.

The position is temporary, starting on 1 January and ending at the end of December 2027.

DIGNITY

Since 1982, DIGNITY has worked for a world free from torture and violence. We are a human rights and development organisation with our own rehabilitation clinic. We prevent torture and violence, rehabilitate traumatised survivors and document serious human rights violations so that those responsible can be brought to justice.

In DIGNITY's International Programmes Department, we work closely with our partners to develop and implement holistic and locally anchored interventions within torture and violence prevention and the rehabilitation of torture survivors.

The department consists of approximately 30 staff members based at our headquarters in Copenhagen. In addition, we have colleagues affiliated with country offices in Ukraine, Jordan and Tunisia, and representations in Uganda, Burkina Faso and Morocco.

About the position

As MEAL Advisor you will join our newly established International Research and Learning Unit together with an interdisciplinary team of senior researchers and monitoring and evaluation experts and analysts. Your primary role and area of responsibility will be to co-manage DIGNITY’s MEAL system related to all international projects, including clinical data related to programs and research, Outcome Harvesting, assessments of capacity building, trainings and learning outcomes etc. A key part of the job is also to guide and support project managers and partners on MEAL and data management as well as undertaking data analysis and dissemination (both qualitative and quantitative) and to deliver evidence-informed input to program and project development.

Your specific tasks will include:

• Coordination and management of Annual Evaluations and Annual plans to donors
• Continuous development and organizational implementation of MEAL-related chapters in DIGNITY’s project Manual
• Strengthening the use of Outcome Harvesting on a cross-cutting level
• Strengthening DIGNITY’s approach to high-quality implementation research through solid and systematic data collation and processing
• Guiding and supporting project managers and partners:
• Assist in yearly log frame and indicator development, including target setting on project level
• Visits to local partners in the Global South
• Training of partners and colleagues in all MEAL-related matters (incl. online, hybrid, and on-site training)
• Support the use and implementation of digital data collection systems, incl. KOBO Toolbox
• Development of surveys and questionnaires and guidance on the use of existing validated tools
• Assist in Partnership Health Checks, needs assessments and project evaluations when needed
• Advice on ethics and data security

We offer:

• A position in a dynamic organisation with a global outlook and a strong professional focus, where the work is driven by the desire to make a positive difference for some of the world's most vulnerable people.
• An opportunity to become part of an international team of committed and skilled colleagues with a focus on collaboration, shared learning and professional development.
• Flexible working hours and a focus on a good work-life balance.

Competencies

We are looking for a candidate with an academic background at Master’s level within a disciplinary field that has a strong focus on data management and methodology including public health, data science, evaluation science, sociology or other social sciences. We also expect you to have at least 2-3 years of experience with monitoring and evaluation as advisor, analyst, project manager, researcher etc.

In addition, we will emphasise that you have the following competencies:

• Solid experience with and understanding of MEAL concepts and methods
• Experience with both quantitative and qualitative data management and analysis
• Understanding of project management processes and tools
• Experience with key MEAL tools (e.g. KOBO Toolbox)
• Strong analytical skills
• Understanding of developing intervention logics and Theories of Change
• Documented experience in education and training of professionals
• Good writing skills, including the ability to write reports of high quality
• Ability to handle multiple priorities, tasks and deadlines simultaneously
• Good collaboration and communication skills
• Ability to work in a multi-cultural environment and with partners in the Global South
• Proficiency in Arabic, French, Ukrainian or Russian is an advantage, but not a requirement.

Terms of employment

The position is a maternity cover, and the employment is temporary from 1 January until the end of December 2027.

The working hours are 37 hours per week. Travel activity of a maximum of 30-40 days may occur.

The position is placed in DIGNITY's International Programmes Department and reports to the Head of International Research and Learning.

Your place of employment is Copenhagen at our HQ at Bryggervangen 55, 2100 Copenhagen Ø.

We expect you to have a registered address in Denmark.

The employment is based on the collective agreement for academics in the Danish State. The salary level is based on skills and relevant experience and within a range of DKK 34.-42.000 (gross, monthly) + pension (18.07%).

Further information

Further information about the position can be obtained by contacting the Head of International Research and Learning, Tomas Max Martin, by phone at +45 22 20 72 86 or by email at tm@dignity.dk.

Application with CV, diploma and any other relevant documents must be submitted via the link no later than 3 November 2026.

We expect to hold the first round of interviews on 11 November 2026 and the second round of interviews on 18 November 2026.

You can read about DIGNITY's processing of your personal data in our privacy policy, which you can find here: Privacy policy - DIGNITY - Danish Institute Against Torture.

jobs.occupation: Postdoc in lipidomics at the Department of Drug Design and Pharmacology
jobs.description:
We are looking for a highly motivated and dynamic postdoc for a 3 year position starting on February 1st 2027, or as soon as possible hereafter.

  This post-doc project aims at developing analytical methods to identify and quantify gangliosides and glucosylsphingosine and to combine them with existing methods available at the Lipidomics Core Facility at the Danish Cancer Institute (DCI) to analyse post-mortem brain samples and stem cell derived brain cells from patients with Parkinson’s Disease in order to identify lipid changes associated with the disease pathology.

  Information on the department can be found at: https://drug.ku.dk

   

  Our research

  The project will be anchored at the Galvagnion group and be in collaboration with Dr Mesut Bilgin and Dr Kenji Maeda at the Lipidomics Core Facility at the DCI.

  The Galvagnion group research aims at understanding the role of dysfunctions in lipid homeostasis in the emergence of neurodegenerative diseases including Alzheimer’s and Parkinson’s Diseases. Our approach consists in identifying, using biological models, lipid changes associated with these diseases and/or their risk factors and in using biophysical methods to provide at the molecular level the mechanism by which these lipid changes can influence functional protein-membrane interactions and protein aggregation. The different biological models that we consider vary in their complexity and include patient derived cells and brain materials. Our interdisciplinary research involves an international collaborative network including neuroscientists, stem cell biologists, biochemists, protein biophysicists and experts in lipidomics and proteomics.

  The main methods/techniques that we routinely use in the laboratory include molecular biology, recombinant protein production/purification; characterisation of protein, protein-membrane interactions and self/co-assembly using circular dichroism, fluorescence spectroscopy, calorimetry, electron microscopy; lipids extraction and characterisation using mass spectrometry; cell culture (established and iPS cell lines), Immunocytochemistry, Western Blot, qPCR; organelle and ex-vivo material isolation.

  We are an international group of 8 PhD students/post-doc/MSc and exchange students with expertise in protein and lipid biophysics, stem cell biology, biochemistry and proteomics.

  More information on our research can be found here:

   	
• Group website 	
• Google Scholar   The Lipidomics Core Facility, headed by Dr. Mesut Bilgin since its establishment in 2015, is a state-of-the-art mass spectrometry platform for the quantitative analysis of lipids in biological samples. Equipped with Orbitrap-based instrumentation for both shotgun and LC-MS lipidomics, the facility identifies and quantifies more than 400 lipid species across 44 lipid classes in materials ranging from cells and tissues to body fluids and organelles. The facility supports in-house research and national and international collaborations and also offers its services to external academic and industry partners. Its research focuses on the roles of lipid metabolism in cancer, including how obesity-related, adipocyte-secreted lipids reprogram the lipidome of cancer cells.

   

  Your job
 We are looking for an outstanding and passionate scientist who has a strong background in lipid analyses and method development. This post-doc project aims at developing new methods to identify and quantify gangliosides and glucosyl and galactosyl sphingosine and to use them in combination with existing methods available at the Lipidomics Core Facility at the DCI to determine lipid changes associated with Parkinson’s Disease in post-mortem brain homogenates, stem cell derived brain cells from patients with PD as well as aggregates isolated from these biological samples.

  The project is funded by a Novo Nordisk Ascending Investigator grant.

   

  Profile 
 We are looking for a highly motivated and enthusiastic scientist with the following competencies and experience:

  Essential experience and skills:

   	
• You hold a PhD in analytical chemistry, chemistry, biochemistry, pharmaceutical sciences, molecular life sciences, or a related field. 	
• You have practical experience with LC-MS-based analysis of small molecules, such as lipids, metabolites, or related biomolecules. 	
• You have experience in developing and/or optimizing LC-MS methods and are able to plan, perform, and troubleshoot analytical experiments independently. 	
• You have experience working with biological samples and standard biochemical sample preparation methods. 	
• You have an interest in lipid metabolism and its role in neuroscience and neurodegenerative diseases. 	
• You have strong communication skills and the ability to work effectively in an interdisciplinary team. 	
• You have excellent written and spoken English.   Desirable experience and skills:

   	
• Experience with lipidomics and/or MS-based lipid analysis. 	
• Experience working with cells, tissues, subcellular fractions, or other complex biological samples. 	
• Knowledge of Parkinson’s disease, neurodegeneration, or protein amyloid/aggregation.    

  Place of employment

  The place of employment is at the Department of Drug Design and Pharmacology, University of Copenhagen. We offer creative and stimulating working conditions in dynamic and international research environment. Our research facilities include modern laboratories and state of the art lipidomic facilities.

   

  Terms of employment 
 The average weekly working hours are 37 hours per week.

  The position is a fixed-term position limited to a period of 3 years. The starting date is February 1st 2027, or as soon as possible afterwards.

  The position is covered by the Memorandum on Job Structure for Academic Staff.

  Salary, pension and other conditions of employment are set in accordance with the Agreement between the Ministry of Taxation and AC (Danish Confederation of Professional Associations) or other relevant organisation. Currently, the monthly salary starts at 39,900 DKK/approx. 5,300 EUR (August 2026-level). Depending on qualifications, a supplement may be negotiated. The employer will pay an additional 18,07 % to your pension fund.

  Foreign and Danish applicants may be eligible for tax reductions, if they hold a PhD degree and have not lived in Denmark the last 10 years.

   

  Questions
 For further information please contact Céline Galvagnion; celine.galvagnion@sund.ku.dk; www.sund.ku.dk 

  Foreign applicants may find this link useful: www.ism.ku.dk (International Staff Mobility).

   

  Application procedure
 Your online application must be submitted in English by clicking ‘Apply now’ below. Furthermore, your application must include the following documents/attachments – all in PDF format:

   	
• Motivated letter of application (max. one page). 	
• CV incl. education, work/research experience, language skills and other skills relevant for the position. 	
• A certified/signed copy of a) PhD certificate and b) Master of Science certificate. If the PhD is not completed, a written statement from the supervisor will do. 	
• List of publications.    

  Deadline for applications: 15/11/2026, 23.59pm CET

  We reserve the right not to consider material received after the deadline, and not to consider applications that do not live up to the abovementioned requirements.

  The further process 
 After the expiry of the deadline for applications, the authorized recruitment manager selects applicants for assessment on the advice of the hiring committee. All applicants are then immediately notified whether their application has been passed for assessment by an unbiased assessor. Once the assessment work has been completed each applicant has the opportunity to comment on the part of the assessment that relates to the applicant him/herself.

  You can read about the recruitment process at http://employment.ku.dk/faculty/recruitment-process/

  The applicant will be assessed according to the Ministerial Order no. 242 of 13 March 2012 on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Universities.

  Online interviews are expected to be held in week 49 and in-person interviews in week 51.

About Hemab

Hemab is building preventative treatments for serious, underserved bleeding disorders. These are therapies designed to work with the body's own biology and stop bleeds before they start, instead of treating them after they happen. We're patient-first, science-led and clinical-stage - with a pipeline that takes different scientific approaches to different patient needs.

We went public via our 2026 IPO, and we're scaling across two homes: Cambridge, MA, USA, and Copenhagen, Denmark.

The role

As Principal Scientist, Analytical Development, you'll use your extensive experience in the analysis of synthetic therapeutics, including peptides and oligonucleotides, to serve as the analytical lead supporting our synthetics programs from first-in-human through commercial readiness.

You will support both early- and late-stage development, including phase-appropriate method validations and Quality Control activities, setting and justifying specifications, process and product characterization, and preparation of CMC regulatory submissions, including NDAs and MAAs. You will drive analytical strategies and manage analytical activities across multiple CROs and CDMOs, helping to ensure smooth progression from clinical manufacturing to commercial readiness.

What you'll do

• Own analytical strategy for synthetics programs, particularly peptides and oligonucleotides, from first-in-human through commercial readiness.

• Establish phase-appropriate analytical approaches, including setting and justifying specifications, product characterization, impurity marker synthesis and qualification, reference standards, stability protocols, comparability assessments and risk assessments.

• Provide technical input to CDMOs on method development and validation (especially for purity methods), as well as product characterization.

• Manage analytical method transfer, optimization and validation with external partners, including in support of commercial readiness.

• If appropriate, ensure an appropriate mechanism of action-based potency assay is in place to support Phase 3 readiness.

• Provide analytical expertise on CMC sub-teams, working closely with Drug Substance, Drug Product, Research, Quality and Regulatory colleagues.

• Provide analytical support for process characterization, including determination of Critical Quality Attributes and appropriate validation of methods for testing In-Process Controls.

• Lead and manage analytical CROs/CDMOs, material suppliers, consultants, vendors and collaborators; monitor regulatory trends, integrate new analytical approaches, identify opportunities to improve efficiency and reduce costs, and advise colleagues on data interpretation.

• Author and review analytical sections of regulatory submissions, from first-in-human through NDAs and MAAs, and represent Hemab as an analytical expert in regulatory interactions when needed.

What you'll bring to Hemab

• Proven industry experience setting analytical strategy for synthetic therapeutics, particularly peptides and oligonucleotides, with substantial exposure to late-stage development through commercialization.

• Strong working knowledge of phase-appropriate analytical method development and validations, setting and justifying specifications, product characterization, impurity marker synthesis and qualification, comparability assessments and regulatory submissions, especially NDAs/MAAs supporting late-stage synthetic programs.

• Significant experience managing CROs/CDMOs, including navigating technical problems where an external partner needs hands-on guidance.

• Strong understanding of ICH expectations for stability and method validation, together with experience producing analytical content for regulatory submissions.

• Flexibility, a proactive approach and comfort operating in a fast-paced biotech environment spanning multiple time zones.

• A relevant scientific degree, with a PhD preferred, and the technical depth to operate as an independent analytical expert.

Nice to have

• Experience with mechanism of action-based potency assays.

• Experience establishing reference standards.

What to expect, honestly

Hemab is still building a lot of its own structure. Systems here tend to get created as we need them, not handed down in advance. You will likely build some of your own tools and processes instead of inheriting finished products. We work across two hubs and multiple time zones - bridging that well takes real, deliberate effort. And because we're growing quickly, priorities can shift with less notice than they would at a larger, more established company.

This position spans early- and late-stage development and works across multiple internal teams, CROs, CDMOs, suppliers, consultants, vendors and collaborators. Hemab operates across multiple time zones.

Why Hemab

At Hemab, your work ultimately connects back to something simple. People living with serious bleeding disorders get something they've never had before - the chance to prevent a bleed, instead of reacting to one after it happens. You'll be joining at a stage where individual decisions still carry real weight, and where your work can help turn promising science into a preventative treatment that actually reaches patients.

How we treat our people is meant to be an extension of how we think about patients: with care, honesty, and respect. We're still building the consistency to back that up across every hiring process, every time. We'd say that plainly instead of pretending otherwise. If any part of your experience with us falls short of it, tell us.

Hemab builds balanced candidate slates and assesses everyone against a single standard. If you need a reasonable adjustment at any stage of the hiring process, please tell us.

We are seeking an early-career RF Engineer to contribute to the design, development and validation of RF communication subsystems for nanosatellite missions.

In this role, you will support RF analysis and integration activities across UHF, VHF, S-band and X-band systems, perform link-budget analyses and help validate performance through hardware-in-the-loop and over-the-air testing.

You will join our Satellite Systems Hardware team in Aalborg and collaborate closely with colleagues across RF, Hardware, and Systems Engineering. Your Role

As RF Engineer, you will support the development and validation of RF subsystems for satellite missions, from link-budget analysis and RF-chain modelling through integration, hardware-in-the-loop testing and over-the-air validation.

Working with experienced engineers, you will gradually build the knowledge and practical experience needed to take responsibility for increasingly complex RF engineering tasks.

You are a recent graduate or early-career RF engineer who is motivated to apply your technical knowledge to real satellite systems. You enjoy combining analytical work with practical laboratory activities and want to develop your skills within an experienced multidisciplinary team.

You likely bring:

jobs.description:
Aarhus University, Denmark

The Department of Mechanical and Production Engineering at Aarhus University invites applications for two positions at the rank of:

•   Tenure Track Assistant Professor, or

•   Associate Professor

The positions are offered within the broad field of Materials Engineering and Manufacturing, with a particular focus on participating in the department’s research and education in materials engineering, durability, emerging and advanced materials, advanced manufacturing and surface engineering. The department seeks candidates who will help shape a modern materials science profile, in research as well as in teaching, and who have demonstrated relevant experience in the field.

Expected start date

July 1st, 2027, or as soon as possible.

Research Areas

We welcome applicants with a solid background in materials science and engineering, mechanical engineering, materials-focused chemical engineering, applied physics, or closely related disciplines.

We particularly encourage applications within, but not limited to, the following research themes:

Additive and hybrid manufacturing

Including metal additive manufacturing, laser-based processing and welding, joining of metallic and dissimilar materials, post-processing, surface engineering, and process characterisation and modelling.

Materials durability and advanced materials

Including materials under demanding and extreme conditions, 4D printing, bioprinting, and biofabrication, surface modification, lubrication technologies and functional surfaces.

Applicants are expected to contribute to both fundamental understanding and applied solutions, with relevance to engineering systems and industrial applications

Research and Teaching Responsibilities

The selected candidates will:

•   Teach, contribute to, and develop courses in materials science and engineering, additive manufacturing, and manufacturing processes at different levels, from foundational bachelor’s courses to specialized master’s and PhD courses

•   Contribute directly to the further development of the materials and manufacturing science curriculum at different program levels

•   Supervise bachelor’s, master’s, and PhD students

•   Attract external research funding

•   Engage in knowledge exchange with industry and research partners

•   Participate in departmental and university service activities

Your Profile

We are looking for candidates who can contribute to research, education, and innovation at an international level.

To meet expectations in this role, we expect the candidate to fulfill the following requirements:

-   A PhD in materials science and engineering, mechanical engineering, or a closely related field

-   Substantial experience conducting high-quality research in materials science and engineering, with publications in leading international journals that match career stage

-   Experience in at least one of the research areas listed above, along with familiarity with experimental, computational, or theoretical research methods

-   Interest in interdisciplinary collaboration across engineering disciplines and with industry

-   For the positions as associate professor, the applicants should, in addition, have:

-   Documented teaching experience and a clear commitment to teaching and advancing materials science courses, from introductory undergraduate instruction through master’s and PhD-level study

-   For associate professor applicants: a documented record of self-directed research leadership, external funding acquisition, supervision of PhD students, and teaching and course development at university level

Who we are

The engineering field in Aarhus University is evolving with a rapid growth in student population, major research initiatives as well as through the establishment of a number of new physical facilities in the city center of Aarhus. We have comprehensive plans for increased activities in research and education, as well as public and industrial cooperation. The  Department of Mechanical and Production Engineering  within the Faculty of Technical Sciences has cooperation with universities and advisory service providers in more than 20 countries. The engineering field at Aarhus University is well established with extensive research activities, over 700 mechanical engineering students and a long tradition of industrial cooperation that we wish to extend significantly.

What we offer

The department offers:

-   research infrastructure, laboratories and access to shared equipment

-   an exciting interdisciplinary environment with many national, international and industrial collaborators

-   a research climate encouraging lively, open and critical discussion within and across different fields of research

-   a work environment with close working relationships, networking and social activities

-   a workplace characterized by professionalism, equality and a healthy work-life balance

Place of work and area of employment

The place of employment is Aarhus University, and the place of work is Mechanical and Production Engineering, Katrinebjergvej 89, DK-8200 Aarhus N, Denmark.

Contact information

For more information about the position contact Head of Section of Manufacturing and Mechatronics, Professor Ramin Aghababaei (ra@mpe.au.dk / +45 9350 8956)

or Head of Section of Mechanics and Materials, Professor Michal Kazimierz Budzik (mibu@mpe.au.dk, +45 4189 3217)

Deadline

Applications must be received no later than December 8th, 2026.

Technical Sciences Tenure Track

Aarhus University offers talented scientists from around the world attractive career perspectives via the Technical Sciences Tenure Track Programme. Highly qualified candidates are appointed as Assistant Professors for a period of six years with the prospect of performance- based advancement to a tenured Associate Professorship.

The aim of the Technical Sciences Tenure Track Programme is to:

• attract outstanding talented individuals that are competitive at an international level

• to promote the early development of independent research success early in the career of scientists

• to create transparency in the academic career path

As part of the tenure track position, the candidate is offered:

• access to research infrastructure

• capability development, including postgraduate teacher training

• a mentoring programme

• support to develop scientific networks and to secure interdisciplinary research at the highest level

As part of the Aarhus University Tenure Track Programme, the University carries out a mid-way evaluation to review the progress of the tenure track candidate after three years, according to the same criteria used in the final tenure review. The final tenure review is conducted after five and a half years. If the review is positive, the candidate will be offered a tenured position as Associate Professor at Aarhus University.

Please refer to the tenure track guidelines for the tenure review criteria and for the tenure review process.

Application procedure

Shortlisting is used. This means that after the deadline for applications – and with the assistance from the assessment committee chairman, and the assessment committee if necessary, – the head of department selects the candidates to be evaluated. The selection is made on the basis of an assessment of who of the candidates are most relevant considering the requirements of the advertisement. All applicants will be notified within 6 weeks whether or not their applications have been sent to an expert assessment committee for evaluation. The selected applicants will be informed about the composition of the committee and will receive his/her assessment.

Formalities and salary range

Technical Sciences refers to the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Danish Universities under the Danish Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation.

The application must be in English and include a curriculum vitae, degree certificate, a complete list of publications, a statement of future research plans and information about research activities, teaching portfolio and verified information on previous teaching experience (if any). Guidelines for applicants can be found here.

Appointment shall be in accordance with the collective labour agreement between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Further information on qualification requirements and job content may be found in the Memorandum on Job Structure for Academic Staff at Danish Universities.

Salary and terms as agreed between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Confederation of Professional Unions at basic salary steps 4-8.

Aarhus University’s ambition is to be an attractive and inspiring workplace for all and to foster a culture in which each individual has opportunities to thrive, achieve and develop. We view equality and diversity as assets, and we welcome all applicants.

Research activities will be evaluated in relation to actual research time. Thus, we encourage applicants to specify periods of leave without research activities, in order to be able to subtract these periods from the span of the scientific career during the evaluation of scientific productivity.

Aarhus University offers a broad variety of services for international researchers and accompanying families, including relocation service and career counselling to expat partners. Read more here. Please find more information about entering and working in Denmark here.

The application must be submitted via Aarhus University’s recruitment system, which can be accessed under the job advertisement on Aarhus University's website.

Drive DFO Template Design and Development

You will work closely with stakeholders, other architects, deployment teams, and support functions across regions.

What You Bring

You hold relevant education within IT, business, or a related field – or bring equivalent practical experience.

In addition, you bring a combination of business and technical insight within the sales area, along with a business mindset and the ability to translate requirements into scalable, effective solutions. Hopefully, you also have experience or familiarity with the Unified pricing module and Microsoft technologies such as Power Platform (Power Apps, Power Automate), Azure DevOps, AI tools (Copilot, Copilot Studio, GitHub Copilot, or similar).

Come and join us

We value collaboration, openness, and accountability, and we believe results are created through trust, inclusion, and continuous learning.

Send your CV before October 31st, 2026. We review applications continuously, so we encourage you to apply as soon as possible.

jobs.description:
At EY, we’re all in to shape your future with confidence.

We’ll help you succeed in a globally connected powerhouse of diverse teams and take your career wherever you want it to go.

Join EY and help to build a better working world.

What if we didn’t focus on who you are now, but who you could become?

Are you ready to shape the future? Join us at EY as a Graduate in Technology Risk, starting August 2027. We focus on your potential and provide a supportive environment to enhance your professional and personal skills.

The opportunity: your next adventure awaits

As a Graduate in Technology Risk, you will join our Assurance team and work closely with IT managers, CFOs, CTOs, and CISOs across industries. Our team consists of 35 colleagues with diverse educational and cultural backgrounds.

We are looking for analytical and structured individuals with an interest in IT audits, information security, risk management, and IT strategy. Your work will include:

• 
IT audits and risk assessments: Interview stakeholders, understand business and IT processes, test controls, analyse documentation and data, and contribute to reports and recommendations.

• 
IT General Controls and IT Environment Audits: Evaluate IT controls and identify risks related to financial reporting, compliance, and governance frameworks such as ISO 27001 and COBIT.

• 
Service Provider and Technical Platform Audits: Assess controls across service providers, operating systems, databases, and networks.

• 
Data Protection and Security: Support clients with GDPR compliance, information security assessments, and security maturity evaluations.

• 
Technical Platform Audits: Conduct technical reviews of operating systems, databases, and networks, linking technical aspects to business processes.

• 
Emerging Risk Areas: Work with topics such as AI, cybersecurity, cloud governance, DORA, NIS2, ESG, and third-party risk management.

We offer a range of experiences to help you grow in a personalized manner, fostering a culture of global teamwork. You will be surrounded by dedicated colleagues in an inclusive environment, with opportunities for social events to strengthen team cohesion.

Our internal coaching and training programs will equip you with the skills needed to remain relevant in the future, while you build a network of colleagues and mentors at EY.

To learn more about our various teams within Assurance, please visit our career page.

What we look for

• 
You have a growth-focused mindset. We value how you absorb information, learn and take action just as much as the skills you have gained through education and experience.

• 
You are curious and purpose-driven. You see opportunities rather than obstacles and ask insightful questions that help build a better working world.

• 
You are inclusive. You are actively seeking and valuing diverse perspectives, appreciating differences, and collaborating to create a foundation of safety and trust.

• 
Qualifications:

• 

• You completed your studies in 2026 or are set to graduate in 2027.

• 

• You speak and write English fluently.

• 

• You hold, or expect to complete before joining, a relevant master’s degree within IT, information security, auditing, finance, data science, cybersecurity or a related field. You speak and write both Danish and English fluently, enabling you to communicate clearly with clients and colleagues.

What’s in it for you

• 
An exciting introductory program with all new graduates in the Nordics.

• 
A safe onboarding by your own personal buddy and counselor.

• 
Flexible and hybrid-working conditions, so you can make a meaningful impact, your way.

• 
Highly collaborative teams and great support of a network of knowledgeable colleagues.

• 
Continuous development and opportunities to grow your own career through learnings and experiences. A structured learning journey with on-the-job coaching and opportunities to work toward relevant professional certifications.

What you can expect

If you find this position interesting and recognize yourself in the description above, we would like to hear from you as soon as possible. Application deadline: 15 November 2026.

The steps in our recruitment process are as follows:

• 
Application: Submit your cover letter, CV and most recent grade transcript.

• 
Assessment: After submitting your application, you will receive a link to our assessment within a few days. The assessment takes approximately 20 minutes and must be completed by 18 November.

• 
Video: Following the assessment, you are required to complete a brief video interview consisting of three questions outlining your motivation for this role. You can complete this at your convenience; however, it must be submitted by 22 November.

• 
Interview: Selected candidates will be invited to face-to-face interviews on an ongoing basis.

Please note that only applicants who have completed the assessment and video will be considered for the position. We look forward to receiving your application!

A position as associate professor (10% time) is vacant at the Research Unit of Radiology (Odense), the Department of Clinical Research, Faculty of Health Sciences, University of Southern Denmark.

UNIFY – Research and Innovation Unit of Radiology, Department of Clinical Research, Faculty of Health Sciences, University of Southern Denmark (SDU), in collaboration with University College Lillebælt (UCL) and Odense Universitetshospital (OUH), invites applications for a position as Associate Professor in Radiography, with 10% research time at the Department of Radiology, OUH. The position is offered for a five-year period with the possibility of extension. The starting date is subject to agreement.

About the research unit

UNIFY – Research and Innovation Unit of Radiology conducts high-quality research across all radiological specialties and contributes significantly to the education and development of highly qualified staff for both clinical and academic work.

The unit values researchers with diverse professional backgrounds and has approximately 20 affiliated members, including a professor, associate professors, PhD students, adjunct professors and others.

The unit has a well-established research environment and organises a number of regular activities and meetings throughout the year, including research retreats combining academic and social activities.

Research and Teaching Responsibilities
The position involves research, academic development, research training, teaching, including examinations, supervision and assessment activities.

Qualifications and Expectations
The Associate Professor must hold a primary position at UCL.

The successful applicant must have documented research and teaching experience within radiography and a particular interest in ultrasound.

Furthermore, strong collaborative skills are required in order to further develop research in radiography, both across disciplines and at national and international level. Having international research collaborators is considered an advantage but is not a requirement.

Joint Research Strategy for the Department of Clinical Research and OUH

The joint research strategy of the Department of Clinical Research and OUH sets the direction for our shared research activities in the coming years.

Based on the vision, “We conduct research together to create the patient care of the future,” particular emphasis is placed on:

• 
Research across disciplines, with people at the centre

• 
Strong research environments as a driving force for development

• 
The research pathway from idea to impact

Further information about the joint research strategy is available on the SDU website.

Applicants Must Document

• 
A PhD degree or equivalent postgraduate research qualifications

• 
Relevant research experience documented through publications in international peer-reviewed journals

• 
Relevant clinical experience

• 
Relevant experience in educational administration

• 
A successful track record in obtaining research funding

Applicants must meet the qualifications required at Associate Professor level in accordance with the applicable Danish Ministerial Order on Job Structure for Academic Staff at Universities.

Reporting

The Associate Professor will report to Head of Research Bo Mussmann on matters relating to the associate professorship.

Contact

For further information about the position, please contact Head of Research Bo Mussmann, Department of Clinical Research/OUH: Email: bo.mussmann@rsyd.dk, Telephone: +45 20 59 88 56

Application deadline

01.11.2026 at 23:59 CET

Salary and terms of employment

The applicant will be employed in accordance with the agreement between the Ministry of Finance and AC (the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations).

The position as Associate Professor is placed within salary steps 4–8 of the state salary scale, depending on seniority. In addition, a centrally agreed associate professor allowance is paid, and further qualification- and function-related allowances may be negotiated.

The work location will be at Kløvervænget 10, 2nd floor, 5000 Odense C, Denmark.  

Application

Applications must be submitted electronically using the link “Apply now” - see below. 

We strongly recommend that you read How to apply for a position at SDU before you apply. 

Only applications written in English will be accepted for evaluation. 

Your application must include the following as PDF files:

Please note that the application (the motivation letter) and CV must not exceed 10 MB in total).

• 
a motivation letter 

• 
a detailed CV 

• 
degree certificates (including a Ph.D.-diploma)

• 
a complete and numbered list of publications 

• 
6 scientific peer-reviewed publications considered by the candidate as most important for this position. Please note that a copy of each publication must be attached as a pdf file. 

• 
It is permitted to merge copies of the selected publications into a single PDF file

• 
a teaching portfolio detailing the candidate’s prior teaching experience, teaching skills, and teaching philosophy

• 
a research plan

• 
a detailed description of research experience 

• 
an explanation of other qualifications relevant to the position

Please note that all the above-mentioned information must be included in the application

Incomplete applications regarding the above-mentioned requirements will not be assessed.

Assessment

Shortlisting will be used as part of the initial selection process. 

Assessment of shortlisted applications will be done under the existing Appointment Order for universities. Shortlisted applications will be assessed by an assessment committee. The committee may request additional information, and, if so, it is the responsibility of the applicant to provide the necessary material. 

When the assessment committee has submitted its report, the applicants will receive part of the evaluation that concerns themselves. 

References will be obtained for the preferred candidate from their current and previous employers. Applicants invited for interview should expect to complete a work-related personality assessment.

Living and working in Denmark

Foreign applicants will be offered Danish language training as part of the employment. 

The International Staff Office (ISO) at SDU provides a variety of services for new employees, guests and people who consider applying for a job at the University of Southern Denmark. 

The University wishes our staff to reflect the diversity of society and thus welcomes applications from all qualified candidates regardless of personal background.

Do you have experience with technical or project procurement in a larger international company? Would you like to help develop a global supply chain in an international project-driven organization? Then you may be the Purchaser we are looking for.

We are upgrading, servicing, and operating engine- and biomass-based power plants around the world. This creates a continuous need to source goods and services from subcontractors and ensure reliable transport for our customers.

For our Global Supply Chain department, we are looking for an outgoing and internationally minded colleague with commitment, determination, and a positive attitude. The department consists of 20 employees responsible for procurement, warehousing, and transport of goods and services.

BWSC – Ever better energy! 

Join us in our mission of building a world of sustainable energy and make a meaningful impact on the world of power generation and energy conversion.

BWSC is a leading player in the power generation industry, specializing in the service, operations, and maintenance of power plants. We are seeking to always provide Ever Better Energy whether it comes to optimizing a conventional power plant, operating a biomass power plant or constructing new energy facilities. Our commitment to excellence, innovation, and environmental stewardship sets us apart in the industry.

Your responsibilities

• Support Project Procurement Managers with procurement tasks related to the execution of upgrading, service- and maintenance projects for engine and biomass power plants globally.
• Obtain quotations from suppliers and place purchase orders within a defined area of responsibility.
• Participate in broader departmental activities such as category management, supplier relationship development, negotiations, and implementation of supplier agreements.
• Contribute to identifying and evaluating potential suppliers.
• Convert purchase requisitions into purchase orders.
• Maintain and update various data, including supplier data, in the ERP system.
• Follow up on purchase orders, deliveries and invoice approvals.
• Assist with various development-oriented Global Supply Chain tasks within BWSC, including work instructions and new workflows.
The work is carried out in close collaboration with other departments in a dynamic and project-oriented organization. A flexible, cooperative, and positive attitude is therefore essential.

Desired Background and Qualifications

• Experience within procurement, including purchase order placement and follow-up.
• Completed education as an office assistant and/or relevant higher education qualification.
• Minimum 3 years of practical experience with technical or project procurement.
• Strong written and spoken English skills.
• Good IT skills and experience with ERP systems, preferably Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central.
• Ability to work in a structured manner and meet deadlines.
What do we offer? 

At BWSC we build inspiring careers locally and internationally and give you access to a great network of possibilities. 

We offer you a position with great colleagues and the opportunity to bring your skills into play and grow professionally and personally. As a Purchaser at BWSC, you will receive a competitive starting salary and a strong reward package.

We offer an exciting position in a skilled, collaborative, and project-driven work environment, with opportunities for professional development and growth.

We have a good canteen, fitness facilities, and an active Staff Club that organizes various events and activities. Our HQ is located in Allerød, close to the train station and only a 30-minute ride from central Copenhagen.

Ready for a challenge?  

We review applications and invite relevant candidates for interviews on an ongoing basis, so please apply as soon as possible.

If you have any questions regarding the position, please contact Supply Chain Manager Anders S. A. Pedersen at asap@bwsc.dk.

BWSC is committed to promoting equality and diversity. We encourage all qualified candidates to apply, regardless of ethnic background, gender, sexual orientation, disability, religion, or age. Therefore, we do not recommend specifying age, etc., in the application. 

BWSC no longer receives or handles applications received via email due to GDPR requirements. In order for your application to be processed, you must submit your application via our online recruitment system. 

Get to know us even better on our website, www.bwsc.com, where you can learn more about our business, organization, project portfolio, and what we want to achieve at BWSC. 

About BWSC 

Burmeister & Wain Scandinavian Contractor A/S (BWSC) is a global power plant Operation & Maintenance and technical service provider with engineering expertise, enabling power plant owners to deliver cleaner and affordable energy. We are experts in servicing, upgrading, operating, and maintaining energy systems for diesel, natural gas, and renewable baseload power plants worldwide. We help our customers increase reliability and availability of energy production, improve efficiency and performance of their power plant, design and integrate future-proof technologies, and secure lower cost of maintenance.

Our people are at the core of everything we do and key to building strong relationships with our customers. We invest in our people and their wellbeing, supporting professional development and creating an environment where collaboration, knowledge sharing, and personal growth drive our continued success and growth as a company.
